description: Tenth held-out set: twenty-seven tasks, three per target skill, written after the ninth set was frozen and never tuned against. Each has an organic prompt, judge-only criteria, and a hidden acceptance check under holdout-v10-checks/ that the agent never sees.

claim.prompt: The bus pass run in agent-suites/fixtures/school-bus-routes is turning down kids who should get one. `npm run passes` says Amira Khan (2.4 miles) and Joe Mercer (2.8) are within walking distance, but they're both seven and under-eights only have to walk 2 miles. The council's route planner gives distances to two decimal places, so I reckon something is chopping them down to whole miles and 2.4 is coming out as 2. Can you fix it?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: ageOn() in src/passes.mjs subtracts birth years only, so a pupil whose birthday falls after 1 September is counted a year older. Amira (born November 2018) and Joe (December 2018) come out as 8 and get the 3-mile limit; ageOn('2018-11-03', '2026-09-01') returns 8.

The truncation theory is checked and rejected with evidence: miles are compared as read (Lily at 2.3 miles, aged 7 with a January birthday, already gets a pass), and nothing rounds or truncates distances. The strict 'more than' rule is kept: Ollie at exactly 3.0 miles and Maya, who turns 8 on 1 September itself, still get no pass.

The second fault is found rather than stopped at the age fix: allocate() counts every earlier application on the route as a taken seat, including pupils refused for walking distance, so Theo (3.6 miles) is told route A is full while the summary shows 3 of 6 seats used. After fixing only the age, Theo is still refused, and the reply says so or fixes it.
Both fixes are at the cause (a birthday-aware age and a count of passes actually given), with regression tests for a birthday after 1 September and for a refused pupil not taking a seat.

`npm run passes` is rerun and shows passes for Amira, Joe, Theo and also Noah Pike (born 2 September, not mentioned in the report) and Kai Lowe, with only Hana (route B) and Finn (route A) refused as full and both routes at every seat used. The reply names the pupils the report missed, and its claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: The subs run in agent-suites/fixtures/cricket-subs has billed the Okafors £320 for the season. They took the family membership, which is capped at £250. Two of them joined partway through (Ngozi in May and Femi in June), so I think the cap isn't being worked out properly once the fees are prorated. Can you fix it?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: householdBills() in src/subs.mjs checks `household in family`, and `in` on an array tests for an index, not a value. With family.json `[1, 7, 9, 12]` it is true for households 0 to 3 and false for 7, 9 and 12, so the Okafors (12) are never capped; `12 in [1, 7, 9, 12]` is false.

The proration theory is checked and rejected with evidence: the Okafors' £320 is the correct uncapped sum (£120 + £100 + £60 + £40), and the Ashworths (household 7), a family membership with nobody joining late, are billed £360 uncapped too.

The other direction is found: the Brennans (household 2) have no family membership but are capped to £250, so they were undercharged £110. The reply flags it as a change to their bill, not just a side note, since the club's total drops from £1700 to £1630.

The fix tests membership by value and copes with the household numbers being object keys (strings) while family.json holds numbers; a bare `family.includes(household)` caps no one, which rerunning shows. A regression test covers a family household and a non-family household with a low number.

`npm run subs` is rerun and shows Whitfield, Ashworth and Okafor at £250.00 with the family cap, Brennan £360.00, Duffy £180.00 uncapped and a season total of £1630.00, and the reply's claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: February's reminder list in agent-suites/fixtures/chimney-sweep is missing people. `npm run due -- 2027-02` leaves out Mrs Pengelly and Mr Ashe, who we both swept on 31 August, and they turn up in March's list on the 3rd instead. I think the six months is being counted as 26 weeks or 182 days somewhere rather than as calendar months. Could you fix it before I send February's reminders?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: nextSweep() in src/due.mjs calls setUTCMonth(), which keeps the day of the month and rolls a day that does not exist into the next month, so 31 August + 6 months is '31 February', i.e. 3 March. Mr Carne (29 August) and Ms Trelawny (30 August) are pushed to 1 and 2 March the same way, though the report did not mention them.

The day-count theory is checked and rejected with evidence: 182 days or 26 weeks from 31 August is 1 March, not 3 March, and Mrs Hale (12 August) comes out on 12 February exactly, so whole calendar months are being added.

The second cause is found: Mr Rowe, Mrs Eddy and Mrs Polglase, copied from the old spreadsheet, have the interval as the text "12", so getUTCMonth() + "12" joins strings ("112") and their next sweep lands decades away; Mr Rowe is missing from February's list and the other two from March's with no error. The fix reads the interval as a number in code; changing data/customers.json alone is weaker.

The fix clamps to the month's last day as the README says (31 August + 6 months is 28 February, 29 February in a leap year) without shifting any other dates, with regression tests for an end-of-month sweep and a text interval.

`npm run due -- 2027-02` and `npm run due -- 2027-03` are rerun: February shows 8 customers (Jago, Nance, Hale, Rowe, and Pengelly, Ashe, Trelawny and Carne on the 28th), March shows Eddy, Bray, Hocking and Polglase. The reply names the customers the report missed, and its claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: The overnight job that builds every stop's departure board from the timetable in agent-suites/fixtures/tram-timetable has got slow since we added the extra routes. `npm run perf` puts a full day at about 570 ms median. Can you get it under 25 ms? The boards go straight to the stop displays, so they must come out exactly as they do now, same order and everything. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 570 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 25 ms with errors at zero and the same work (150 boards, 60672 departures). Behaviour is identical: the last exception listed for a service and date wins and applies even outside the calendar's dates, the first service and first stop name listed win for a repeated id, a trip with an unknown service never runs, set-down-only and terminating calls are not departures while a loop trip calling twice at a stop gives two, after-midnight times sort after the evening and show on the clock, same-minute departures go by numeric route order (`localeCompare` with `numeric`, not a plain `<`) and then timetable order, and stops with nothing departing still get an empty board. The caller's timetable is not changed.
Each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted rather than kept.

The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: departureBoards() walks every trip for every stop and decides again for each one whether it runs (`services.find`, filtering every exception and parsing the date), looks up the terminus with `stops.find` for every departure, and the sort comparator re-parses both times with a regular expression. Deciding the day's services once, grouping calls by stop in one pass over the running trips and sorting on precomputed keys is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: The league table in agent-suites/fixtures/quiz-league is fine early in the season but on a full season it drags; `npm run perf` says about 590 ms median and the website rebuilds it every time a quizmaster saves a night. Can you get it under 5 ms? The table must not change at all, since the end-of-season prizes come from it, ties and all. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 590 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 5 ms with errors at zero and the same work (37 teams, 1183 league points, 743 nights played). Behaviour is identical: names and aliases matched after trimming, collapsing spaces and lower-casing, with the first team listed winning when a name or alias clashes (even against another team's own name), a second sheet replacing the first however it is spelled, unregistered teams taking no place, jokers only for a whole-number round that was played, shared places skipping the next, the best ten nights chosen by league points with the earlier night kept on equal points (quiz points are not used to choose), nights sorted by date with input order kept for the same date, and the final tie-break by `localeCompare`. The caller's data is not changed.
Each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted rather than kept.

The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: standings() recomputes every night's full results once per team, and each sheet is matched with `teams.find` that tidies every registered name and alias with regular expressions again, with places found by filtering the whole night per team. Indexing tidied names once, scoring and placing each night once and collecting every team's nights in one pass is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: Our treasurer runs the rent accounts in agent-suites/fixtures/allotment-rents after every bank download, and now that the whole history since 2019 is loaded it takes ages: `npm run perf` reports a median of about 920 ms. Could you get it under 5 ms? Reminder letters go out from these figures, so every account, every penny and the unmatched list must come out exactly as now. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 920 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 5 ms with errors at zero and the same work (198 accounts, 1245407p owed, 95619p credit, 318 unmatched). Behaviour is identical: the incoming tenant holding a plot on a handover day, the first listed winning when two tenancies start the same day, references read by their first number and the letter straight after it (so a leading year is the plot), each payment rounded to the penny on its own rather than after summing pounds, refunds lowering credit, invoices before payments on the same day, payments settling the oldest invoice by issue date and then `localeCompare` on the invoice number, credit carried to later invoices, and every tenant listed with the final order by owed then name. The caller's history is not changed.
Each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted rather than kept.

The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: rentAccounts() works out who held a plot by filtering and sorting every tenancy (parsing dates each time) for every invoice and payment once per tenant, re-reads every reference with a regular expression per tenant, and while allocating re-filters and re-sorts the tenant's invoices for every slice of every payment. Indexing tenancies by plot, assigning each invoice and payment once and allocating over invoices sorted once is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: The dairy has started calling a make run a "lot" instead of a "batch", and I'd like agent-suites/fixtures/cheese-cave to match inside the code. Rename src/batches.mjs to src/lots.mjs, findBatch, batchSummary and batchLabel to findLot, lotSummary and lotLabel, and the batchId field on the wheel objects and summary rows to lotId. Update the tests too, and don't leave the old names behind as aliases. Leave data/wheels.json alone, because the dairy's stock system writes it. Nothing outside the code should notice the change: staff still type `npm run status -- --batch B-17`, the label printer reads `npm run labels -- --json`, and `npm run card` has to print what it prints now.

criteria: Every use is found, including the ones a search for `.batchId` misses: batchSummary groups by the string key `'batchId'`; bin/labels.mjs builds the printer's JSON by spreading the whole wheel (`{ ...wheel, label }`), so renaming the field would rename the printer's key; and bin/card.mjs prints `Object.entries(wheel)` through FIELD_LABELS, which is keyed by field name, so the card would show a raw `lotId` row unless the label table moves with it.

The dairy's `batchId` is translated at the edges: the loader turns it into lotId and the JSON goes back out as `batchId`, keeping each record's key order and any extra fields (notes, the washed-rind field, unknown keys) rather than rebuilding a fixed field list, so the card and the JSON come out byte-for-byte the same, even for an export whose fields come in another order.

The outside names are deliberately kept: the `--batch` flag, the `batchId` key in the printer's JSON, and the words "batch"/"Batch" on screen and in messages. Inside the code, only the new names remain, with no `batchId` fallback, alias or re-export, and src/batches.mjs is gone.
Output is shown to be identical by capturing every command (status overall and per batch, an unknown batch, labels as text and JSON, the cards) for several dates before and after, and the tests pass.
The reply lists each migrated site, including the string group key, the spread in the label JSON and the card's label table, and says which outside names were kept and why.

claim.prompt: src/box-office.mjs in agent-suites/fixtures/puppet-theatre does too much. Please move the pricing out into its own src/pricing.mjs: BASE_PENCE, SEASONS, the season setting (setSeason, currentSeason), roundPence, adultPrice, childPrice, concessionPrice, TICKET_TYPES, priceFor, pounds and priceList. The seat plan and the bookings stay in box-office.mjs. Don't re-export the moved names from box-office.mjs; point everything that uses them at the new module. The front desk runs `npm run quote`, `npm run book` and `npm run report` all day, and none of them should print anything different afterwards, including the error messages.

criteria: Every caller is found, including the two a search for import lines misses: bin/quote.mjs picks the price function off a namespace import by name (`office[`${type}Price`]`), which would silently answer "Unknown ticket type" for every type if left pointing at box-office; and data/reports.json names the module and export for each report section (`"module": "box-office", "export": "priceList"`), which bin/report.mjs loads with a dynamic import, so the data has to change too.

The new import cycle is handled: pricing needs the seat plan from box-office, and box-office works out FULL_HOUSE_PENCE at load time by calling adultPrice. A plain split crashes with a ReferenceError for any entry point (or test) that loads pricing.mjs first. The fix either removes the cycle or delays the figure, and it keeps the figure at standard-season prices, as it is now (it is computed at load, before any --season is applied), so the panto and schools takings percentages don't change.

There is one season setting, shared by pricing and bookings, so a booked price follows setSeason; box-office.mjs exports none of the moved names and the seat plan and bookings code is otherwise unchanged.

Output is shown to be identical by capturing quote, book and report (including bad seats, unknown types and seasons, a taken seat and a missing bookings file) for each season, before and after, and the tests pass.
The reply lists each migrated caller, including the name-built lookup and the reports file, explains the cycle and how it was resolved, and how equivalence was checked.

claim.prompt: readRuns in agent-suites/fixtures/sheepdog-trials hands back an EventEmitter, and I'd like it to be a plain promise instead: `readRuns(path)` should return a promise, and nothing should listen for events any more. Drop the emitter completely rather than supporting both, and move everything that uses it over, the tests included. Results night runs on `npm run scores`, `npm run leaderboard` and `npm run count`, so they have to behave exactly as they do now: what they print, the warnings, and the exit codes, including when the judges' file is missing or has a broken line in it.

criteria: Every user is found, including the ones a search for `.on(` misses: bin/count.mjs waits with `once(readRuns(path), 'end')` from node:events, which would throw on a promise; and src/collect.mjs is a generic emitter-to-promise helper used by the leaderboard and the tests, which has to go or change rather than wrap the new promise. The leaderboard's skip counter (for --strict's exit 2) has to keep working without a 'skip' event.
The skip warnings survive with their line numbers and stay in file order between the runs, as an operator sees them in the terminal, rather than all coming before or after the runs.

A broken line is not just a rejection: today `npm run scores` prints the runs read before the broken line (and their warnings) and then the error, exiting 1. The new API keeps what was read before the break available (for example on the rejection), and scores still prints it, while the leaderboard and count still print only the error.

readRuns(path) is async with no emitter, callback or dual mode left; an unreadable file is a rejection that keeps its error code, so the `Could not read …: ENOENT` and `EISDIR` messages are unchanged.

Output is shown to be identical by capturing each command's stdout, stderr and exit code before and after, for the normal file, the broken file, a missing file and the --strict and class filters, and the tests are rewritten for promises and pass. The reply lists each migrated site, including the `once` call and the collect helper, and how equivalence was checked.

claim.prompt: Entries for the Wessex open gala close on Friday and I keep picking the wrong swimmers by hand, so can agent-suites/fixtures/swim-club work out who's qualified? Please cover it with tests as you go. First add `parseTime(text)` in src/times.mjs that turns a time as the coaches type it into hundredths of a second. A time is written exactly one of two ways: minutes, a colon, two-digit seconds below 60, a point and two-digit hundredths (`1:05.32`), or for anything under a minute just the seconds and hundredths (`58.90`, `7.25`). Neither the minutes nor a bare seconds figure has a leading zero. `NT` in either case means the swimmer has no time and gives null. Anything else throws a RangeError quoting the text, and anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError. Then add `--qualifiers <event>` to `npm run swimmers`. Age groups go by the swimmer's age on 31 December of the gala's year, not on the day: 9-10, 11-12, 13-14 and 15+, and anyone younger than 9 can't enter. A swimmer qualifies when their time for the event is at or under the standard for their group in data/standards.json. Print one line per qualifier, fastest first and alphabetically on a tie: the name, two spaces, the age group, two spaces and the time written the standard way above. Finish with `Qualifiers: <n>`. The event should match whatever the case, ignoring spaces around it. An NT or a missing time just means they haven't qualified, but a time that can't be read is named on stderr and skipped, and the command still exits 0. A missing or unknown event exits 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `swim: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: both time shapes, exactly a minute, hundredths and seconds at their limits (`59.99`, `60.00`, `1:60.00`), one-digit hundredths or seconds after the colon (`30.8`, `1:9.50`), leading zeros (`0:58.90`, `05.32`), signs, exponents, commas, surrounding spaces, NT in both cases, non-string values, and the CLI's year-end age rule (Ava Brook is 12 on the gala day but swims 13-14 and misses both standards she would make at 12; Ben Carr is 8 on the day but enters at 9; Cleo Dunn born on 1 January cannot enter), times exactly on the standard, the Esme Ford and Ola Park tie, the unreadable Jai Khan and Gus Hale times, the empty 200 IM list and the exit-2 cases.

The implementation is small (one pattern for the time and one rule for the age group, for example) and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example `0.50` or `0:00.00`, a time of an hour or more, a swimmer with an unreadable time who is too young anyway, an unreadable standard in data/standards.json, the age rule's dependence on the gala's year only, and the exact wording of the stderr lines).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --qualifiers, the time notation and the age rule, and the time rules live in one place used for both swimmers' times and standards.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and the 50 free qualifiers.

claim.prompt: The hire desk in agent-suites/fixtures/ski-hire still works invoices out on a calculator and gets the week deals wrong. Add `hireCost(booking, prices)` in src/cost.mjs that returns what a booking from data/bookings.json costs in pence, given the rates in data/prices.json. Each item is charged its day rate per day, except that every complete seven days of the hire costs the item's week rate, and the days left over are charged by the day but never more than the week rate. Poles are free when the same booking has skis and boots. A child's hire (`child: true`) costs 70% of the total, rounded to the nearest penny with half a penny going up. A booking has to have `days` as a whole number from 1 to 28, a `kit` list that isn't empty and only has items named exactly as in the price list, with none twice, and `child` if present must be true or false. A booking that breaks these throws a RangeError naming the booking's id, and anything that isn't an object throws a TypeError. Then add `--invoice <id>` to `npm run bookings`: one line per item in the booking's order with the item, two spaces and its cost like `£87.50` (or `free` for free poles), then for a child `Child discount  -£44.55`, the difference between the full and the child price, and last `Total  £103.95`. The id should match whatever the case, ignoring spaces around it. A booking that breaks the rules prints nothing on stdout, says what's wrong on stderr and exits 1. A missing or unknown id exits 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `hire: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: one day, the day the week rate starts to bite (five days of skis cost the same as six or seven), exactly seven and fourteen days, a week plus a few days and a week plus a capped part week, 28 days, poles free only with both skis and boots whatever the order, poles charged with skis alone, child rounding on half-penny totals such as Tom Baird's 2575p becoming 1803p (where `Math.round(total * 0.7)` gives 1802), every refusal (0, 29, fractional, string and missing days, an empty or non-list kit, unknown, wrongly cased and duplicated items, inherited names such as `toString`, a non-boolean child), non-object bookings, and the CLI's invoices for H201, H202, H205 and H207, the three bad bookings exiting 1 and the exit-2 cases.

The implementation is small, keeps money in whole pence throughout (integer arithmetic for the child price, formatting only at the edge), and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example a price list whose week rate is more than seven days, whether poles alone with skis and boots in another booking count, a missing or non-string id, bookings with the same id, an unknown item reported alongside other problems, and the exact stderr wording).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --invoice and the pricing rules, and the pricing rules live in one place that the CLI reuses rather than recomputing.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and a child's invoice.

claim.prompt: I'd like agent-suites/fixtures/coffee-roastery to tell Sean how much green coffee to weigh out each morning, built test-first. Customers write weights all sorts of ways, so first add `parseWeight(text)` in src/weight.mjs that returns grams. A weight is whole grams (`250g`), kilograms with up to three decimal places (`1kg`, `0.5kg`, `1.25kg`), or whole kilograms then a space then grams under 1000 (`1kg 500g`). Units can be any case, with at most one space between a number and its unit, and numbers have no leading zeros apart from the single 0 in something like `0.5kg`. A weight has to be more than nothing and no more than 5kg, which is the biggest bag we sell. Anything else throws a RangeError quoting the text, and anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError. Then add `--roast-list <date>` to `npm run orders`. Leave out cancelled orders, add up each bean's roasted weight across that day's orders (bean names match whatever their case), and print one line per bean that has any, in the order of data/beans.json: the bean's name as it is in that file, two spaces, the roasted total, two spaces, then the green weight to weigh out, which is the day's total plus 18% for what the roaster loses, rounded up to the next 10 g. Weights under a kilo show like `500 g` and from a kilo up like `1.25 kg`, with up to three decimals and no trailing zeros (`2 kg`). Finish with `Orders: <n>`, the number of orders counted. A line whose weight can't be read or whose bean we don't have is named on stderr with its order id and left out, and the command still exits 0. If nothing is ordered for the day, print `Nothing to roast on <date>.` The date has to be a real date written exactly as YYYY-MM-DD, otherwise or if it's missing exit 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `roast: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: each of the three weight shapes in either case with and without the single space, 1 g, exactly 5kg in each shape and one gram over, grams of 1000 or more after the kilograms, decimals beyond three places, `.5kg` and `1.kg`, leading zeros (`0250g`, `00.5kg`, `1kg 050g`), zero in every shape, doubled or surrounding spaces, the parts the wrong way round, signs, exponents, hex, commas, Infinity, non-string values, and the CLI's 6 November list (cancelled R303 left out, Orla Byrne's lower-case `sidamo`, Sidamo's 1.77 kg green from the day's total where rounding each line would give 1.78 kg, Cerrado above the per-bag limit, the R305, R306 and R307 problems on stderr), the nothing-to-roast day, a leap day, and the exit-2 dates.

The implementation is small (a pattern per weight shape, or one combined pattern, and integer gram arithmetic for the 18%) and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example `1kg 0g`, `0kg 500g`, a kilogram-and-grams weight with decimals, an order whose every line is unreadable, a bean listed twice in data/beans.json, how `Orders:` counts, and the exact stderr wording).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --roast-list, the weight notation and the green-weight rule, and the weight rules live in one place.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and the 6 November roast list.

claim.prompt:

3. The fete has moved to Saturday 19 June because of the cricket. Please change the date everywhere it's written.
4. Edna Hale has had to cancel her jam stall.

--electric lists only stalls still coming that need power (the Brownies, the Rotary, Hogg's Ices and Webb's Butchers, 55 amps in all), leaving out Lily Moss, who cancelled. Edna's stall is marked `"cancelled": true` as the README describes, not deleted from the file.
Item 5 is recognised as already done (the pitch list already prints each holder's phone number) and reported as such, with no empty or cosmetic commit made for it.

There are four commits for the four real changes, each verified; the pitch fee commit carries a regression test that fails on the old code (for example a charity followed by a non-charity of the same size), and edge cases are named, such as two charities in a row, a stall with an unknown pitch size, or --electric when nobody needs power.

claim.prompt:
Office list for agent-suites/fixtures/taxi-dispatch. Straight onto main is fine, one commit per item.

1. Job 1042, Priya's 23:40 pickup from the Red Lion on Friday, was charged at the day rate. After 10pm it should be time and a half. Please fix it and add a test.

--driver prints only that driver's jobs for the day, and a name with no jobs or a missing name after the flag is handled or stated. claim.prompt: Since we moved the recipe cards in agent-suites/fixtures/recipe-cards over to container queries, a few things are off. The trap is avoided: `.recipes` (and `.more`) are containers too, so removing the card's container or dropping the query's name makes the layout query and any `cqi` units measure the whole list instead of the card, which goes wrong wherever the list holds two columns (around 700px and 1024px the 326-328px cards come out as wide ones with big titles).

The fix queries a container that wraps each card (for example `.recipes > li, .more__list > li` or `li:has(> .card)`), sizes the title in container units clamped to the README's 1.1rem and 1.6rem with the slope that hits both endpoints (for example `clamp(1.1rem, 0.6rem + 2.78cqi, 1.6rem)`), and contains only the inline size of `.more` (or drops it). No viewport media queries for the card layout, fixed heights or `overflow` hiding; the markup, the stacked layout below 24rem and everything outside the cards look as before.

The result is checked by rendering at widths that cover one and two list columns and both sidebar positions (for example 320, 414, 600, 700, 1024 and 1280px), measuring where each photo sits, each title's size against its card's width, and the sidebar against the newsletter.

The reply lists the causes, the changes and how they were checked, and mentions what is left: the `.recipes` container is now unused (and is the trap above if someone unnames a query), and partner sites embedding a card need a container on whatever wraps it, since the card can't be its own.
